title: Date and time
theory:
### `java.time` first
Avoid legacy `Date` / `Calendar` in new code. Model instants on the UTC timeline with `Instant`, civil dates with `LocalDate`, wall-clock times with `LocalTime`, and civil datetimes without offset using `LocalDateTime`.

When zoning matters, use `ZonedDateTime` or convert carefully with `ZoneId`. Duration (`Duration`) covers day-time quantities; `Period` models calendar-aware day/month/year differences.

### Formatting and parsing
`DateTimeFormatter` is immutable and thread-safe; define explicit patterns or built-in ISO formats. Parse lazily only after validating input length and charset.

```java
ZoneId zone = ZoneId.of("Europe/Berlin");
ZonedDateTime meeting = ZonedDateTime.of(
    LocalDate.of(2026, 5, 16),
    LocalTime.of(14, 30),
    zone
);
String text = meeting.format(DateTimeFormatter.ISO_OFFSET_DATE_TIME);
```

exercises.title: Create a Time
exercises.description: Use time.Date to create a time.Time value for January 1, 2024, 12:00:00 UTC. Print it using System.out.System.out.printlnln.
exercises.starter_code:
import java.time.*;
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) {} }
hints: `ZonedDateTime.of(2024,1,1,12,0,0,0,ZoneOffset.UTC)` and format to match `2024-01-01 12:00:00 +0000 UTC` using `DateTimeFormatter` + string tweak as in solution.

exercises.title: Time Components
exercises.description: Create a time for March 15, 2023, 14:30:00 at location Asia/Tokyo. Print the year, month, day, hour, minute, and weekday.
exercises.starter_code:
import java.time.*; import java.time.format.TextStyle; import java.util.Locale;
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) {} }
exercises.expected_output:
Year: 2023
Month: March
Day: 15
Hour: 14
Minute: 30
Weekday: Wednesday

exercises.title: Time Duration
exercises.description: Create a duration of 2 hours and 30 minutes using time.Duration. Print it using System.out.System.out.printlnln. Also compute 500 * time.Millisecond and System.out.println it.
exercises.starter_code:
import java.time.Duration;
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) {} }
hints: `Duration.ofHours(2).plusMinutes(30)`; print duration parts matching `2h30m0s` pattern and `500ms` line.

exercises.title: Parse Time
exercises.description: Use time.Parse to parse the string "2024-06-15 09:30:00" with layout "2006-01-02 15:04:05". Print the parsed time and check if there's an error.
exercises.starter_code:
import java.time.*;
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) {} }
hints: `LocalDateTime.parse` with `DateTimeFormatter` or ISO-like pattern; append UTC offset formatting per expected string.

exercises.title: Format Time
exercises.description: Create a time for July 4, 2024, 16:00:00 UTC. Use System.out.System.out.printlnln to System.out.println it with Java's standard layout. Then use t.Format with a custom layout to System.out.println "07/04/2024".
exercises.starter_code:
import java.time.*; import java.time.format.DateTimeFormatter; import java.util.Locale;
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) {} }
hints: `DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("MM/dd/yyyy")` and full English date line for July 4, 2024 UTC.

exercises.title: Time Before and After
exercises.description: Create two time values and use Before() and After() to compare them. Print which one comes first.
exercises.starter_code:

public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) {} }
exercises.expected_output:

December 31 is after January 1: true
hints: `isBefore` / `isAfter` on two `ZonedDateTime` instances with the provided messages.
